claim: MIGE converts captured ideas into orchestrated plans and deployments.
MIGE combines Bitemporal Total System Map (BTSM) with Harmonised Verifiable Cognitive Architecture (HVCA) to turn human intent into auditable, deployable systems.
BTSM provides living inventory of every subsystem, dependency, and policy pack with Minimal-Perfect-Details (MPD) including purpose, capabilities, interfaces, dependencies, and lifecycle.

HVCA employs three-mind neuro-symbolic loop: Mind 1 (Meta-Optimizer) shapes vision tensor, Mind 2 (Context Retriever) gathers context with DVNS and REX-RAG, Mind 3 (Constraint Enforcer) ensures feasibility.

MIGE pipeline stages include seed and vision tensor (g_vision_fit >= 0.90), trunk indexing (g_trunk_coherence, g_scope_coverage), branch variants (g_variant_parity, g_budget_guard), leaf proofs (g_symbolic_consistency, g_test_parity), and evolution controls (g_two_key, g_rollback_ready).

MIGE enforces quality gates at every pipeline stage with VisionFit cosine alignment >= 0.90, lineage completeness >= 95%, blast-radius false negatives = 0, replay success rate >= 99%, and idea-to-deploy lead time <= 14 days.
Every artifact produced by MIGE must be an atomic, witnessed commit with traceability over cleverness, ensuring evidence-first evolution keeps AIM-OS safe to scale.

MIGE integrates with memory layer (CMC stores MPD payloads), planning layer (ideas registry), execution layer (APOE templates), governance layer (Two-Key workflow), and automation (SEG witness packets).
MIGE idea scoring uses four dimensions: Impact (40%), Confidence (30%), Effort (20%), Readiness (10%) with composite score formula.
MIGE template system enables rapid instantiation with quality gates, SEG anchors, and HHNI node updates.
